trickyParts: The leading-zero fix is a refusal, not a conversion: the check does not try to read `032000` as 13312, because a tree that writes it is one no reader can be sure of — Go reads octal, a TypeScript module rejects it, and the right answer is the existing 'declares no <const> this check can read' refusal, which tells the author to restore a plain decimal.

`attached_comment` enters a block comment from its closing line and consumes upward to the line that opens it, so a block is credited however its inner lines are written; it then keeps walking, so a `//` run above a block still counts. A `const (` opener is transparent, but a previous member of the group is not, which is what stops the walk from swallowing an earlier constant's comment in the real embed.go.

`fatal()` ends the run at the first structural failure, so a tree with two unreadable files names one. That is the sibling checks' convention (check-zod-version.sh, check-bun-workspace-manifests.sh, check-gh-version.sh) and deliberate: every finding after an unread file would be a guess. The findings a reader wants listed together — the comparison and the four cross-references — still accumulate and still end with the `::error::<N> problem(s)` summary.

Splitting on `\n` rather than `str.splitlines()` keeps a CRLF file matching the declaration patterns only because each line's trailing `\r` is dropped; without that the `$` anchor would fail on every Windows-checkout line.
